title: Refraction and Lenses
seo_title: Grade 10 Science (SNC2D): Refraction and Lenses Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Refraction and the index of refraction; total internal reflection and the critical angle; images formed by converging and diverging lenses, using ray diagrams and the thin lens equation; and optical devices and the human eye. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand E: Light and Geometric Optics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on refraction and lenses: the index of refraction, Snell's law, total internal reflection, converging and diverging lenses, the thin lens equation and the eye. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: n = c/v: light slows down and bends in a denser medium.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light bends (refracts) when it changes speed at a boundary. The index of refraction n = c/v (water 1.33, glass about 1.50). Going into a medium with a higher n, light bends towards the normal; going into a lower n, it bends away. Past the critical angle, it is totally internally reflected.

A converging (convex) lens brings parallel rays to a focus; a diverging (concave) lens spreads them out. Use ray diagrams or 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ and M = −dᵢ/d₀. The eye uses its cornea and lens to focus a real, inverted image on the retina; glasses correct near- and far-sightedness.

Example

Light travels at 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a plastic. Index of refraction?

n = 3.0 × 10⁸ ÷ 2.0 × 10⁸

Answer: 1.5

Example

A converging lens, f = 5.0 cm, object at 15 cm. Image distance?

1/dᵢ = 1/5 − 1/15 = 2/15

Answer: 7.5 cm

Common mistakes

  • Bending the ray the wrong way at the boundary.
  • Thinking total internal reflection happens going into a denser medium.
  • Using a converging lens to correct near-sightedness.

faq.q: Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
faq.a: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water, so the straw appears in a different place.
Their high index of refraction gives a small critical angle, so light is reflected many times inside.

items.q: Light passes from air into diamond (refractive index 2.42) at an angle of incidence of 50°. What is the angle of refraction?
Leah notices: “A pencil in a glass of water looks broken at the water's surface.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
Light bends as it passes from water into air.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Noah notices: “Eyeglasses help a person see clearly.” What explains this?
c: The lenses bend light so it focuses on the back of the eye.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into water at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: Emma notices: “Raindrops make a rainbow when the Sun is behind you.” What explains this?
c: Sunlight bends and splits into colours inside the drops.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Light travels at 2.00 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
A ray enters crown glass (refractive index 1.52) from air and is refracted at 30° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.52 × sin 30°, so i = 49.5°.

items.q: Emma notices: “A fish in a pond is not exactly where it appears to be.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
Light bends at the water's surface, so the fish's image shifts.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray of light leaves a glass block into air at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: Light travels at 1.24 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
The refractive index of perspex is 1.5. What is the speed of light in perspex? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
Nathan notices: “A hot road looks wet in the distance on a summer day.” What explains this?
c: Light bends as it passes through hot and cooler layers of air.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray enters crown glass (refractive index 1.52) from air and is refracted at 20° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.52 × sin 20°, so i = 31.3°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 60° and an angle of refraction of 35°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 60° ÷ sin 35° = 1.51.

items.q: Noah notices: “A glass prism spreads white light into a band of colours.” What explains this?
c: Each colour bends by a different amount in the glass.
Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: Ethan notices: “A magnifying glass makes letters look bigger.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
The curved lens bends light rays toward each other.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 40° and an angle of refraction of 25°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 40° ÷ sin 25° = 1.52.

items.q: The refractive index of diamond is 2.42. What is the speed of light in diamond? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)

It speeds up and bends towards the normal.

items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: Light travels inside a plastic (critical angle 45.6°) and hits the surface with air at 30° to the normal. What happens?
c: It passes straight through without bending.
Most of it is refracted out into the air, bending away from the normal.
items.e: Total internal reflection happens only when light goes from a denser medium to a less dense one and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a tank 50 cm deep filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.50. How deep does it appear from above?
items.e: Apparent depth = real depth ÷ n = 33.3 cm.

items.e: Total internal reflection happens only when light goes from a denser medium to a less dense one and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.

items.q: Light in air hits acrylic (n = 1.49) at an angle of incidence of 35°. Calculate the angle of refraction.
Why are reflecting telescopes preferred for large telescopes?
c: mirrors have no chromatic aberration and are easier to support
items.e: e.g. Cassegrain telescopes.

A coin lies at the bottom of a tank 20 cm deep filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.33. How deep does it appear from above?
items.e: Apparent depth = real depth ÷ n = 15.0 cm.

c: It passes straight through without bending.
Most of it is refracted out into the air, bending away from the normal.
items.e: Total internal reflection happens only when light goes from a denser medium to a less dense one and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.

items.q: The refractive index of crown glass is 1.52. What is its critical angle?
Which colour is deviated most by a glass prism?
items.e: Glass has the highest refractive index for violet.

A coin lies at the bottom of a tank 60 cm deep filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.33. How deep does it appear from above?
items.e: Apparent depth = real depth ÷ n = 45.1 cm.

items.q: The refractive index of a plastic is 1.4. What is its critical angle?
An object is 9 cm from a converging lens with a focal length of 12 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(12) − 1/9, so dᵢ = −36 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: An object is 9 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −20 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−20) − 1/9, so dᵢ = −6.21 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 25 cm. An object is 37.5 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?
c: real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
items.e: 2F is at 50 cm, so the object is between F and 2F.

items.q: A diverging lens forms an image 4.5 cm on the same side as the object (virtual) when the object is 45 cm away. What is the focal length?
A diverging lens (f = −25 cm) forms an image of an object placed 6 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = −4.84 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(−4.84) ÷ 6 = 0.806. M is positive: the image is upright.

items.q: An object is 24 cm from a converging lens with a focal length of 25 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(25) − 1/24, so dᵢ = −600 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: A diverging lens forms an image 4 cm on the same side as the object (virtual) when the object is 20 cm away. What is the focal length?
An object is 45 cm from a converging lens with a focal length of 25 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(25) − 1/45, so dᵢ = 56.2 cm. A positive dᵢ is a real image.

items.q: A diverging lens (f = −20 cm) forms an image of an object placed 36 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = −12.9 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(−12.9) ÷ 36 = 0.357. M is positive: the image is upright.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 12 cm. An object is 6 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?
c: real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
items.e: 2F is at 24 cm, so the object is between F and the lens.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 5 cm. An object is 20 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?
c: no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
items.e: 2F is at 10 cm, so the object is beyond 2F.

items.q: An object is placed between F and the lens in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
items.e: Object between F and the lens: image virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object. Used in a magnifying glass.

items.q: An object is 15 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −5 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−5) − 1/15, so dᵢ = −3.75 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: Which device uses a converging lens with the object at 2F?
c: a photocopier making a same-size copy
a spotlight making a parallel beam
items.e: Object at 2F: image real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is 40 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?
c: no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
items.e: 2F is at 40 cm, so the object is at 2F.

items.q: An object is placed beyond 2F in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
items.e: Object beyond 2F: image real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side. Used in a camera.

items.q: An object 8 cm tall is 6 cm from a converging lens (f = 12 cm). How tall is the image? (A negative height means inverted.)
items.e: dᵢ = −12 cm, M = −dᵢ/d₀ = 2, so hᵢ = M × h₀ = 16 cm.

items.q: Where must the object be placed for a converging lens to give an image that is real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side?
items.e: Object between F and 2F: image real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side.

items.q: An object is placed at 2F in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
items.e: Object at 2F: image real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side. Used in a photocopier making a same-size copy.

items.q: Which device uses a converging lens with the object at F?
c: a spotlight making a parallel beam
a photocopier making a same-size copy
items.e: Object at F: image no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity).

items.q: An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length 160 cm and an eyepiece of 10 cm. What is its magnifying power in normal adjustment?
items.e: m = fo/fe = 16.0; the tube length is 170 cm.

items.q: What is the angular magnification of a simple microscope (magnifying glass) of focal length 5 cm when the image is at the near point, 25 cm?
What is the angular magnification of a simple microscope (magnifying glass) of focal length 2.50 cm when the image is at the near point, 25 cm?
What does laser eye surgery change?
c: the length of the optic nerve
the shape of the cornea, so light focuses on the retina
items.e: Reshaping the cornea changes how much it bends light.

items.q: A prism of angle 60° gives a minimum deviation of 38°. What is the refractive index of its glass?

Which part of the eye focuses light onto the retina?
c: the lens (with help from the cornea)
items.e: The cornea does most of the bending; the lens adjusts the focus.

items.q: Which device uses a converging lens to make a real image on a sensor?
items.e: Like the eye, a camera focuses a real, inverted image.

items.q: A prism of angle 60° gives a minimum deviation of 32°. What is the refractive index of its glass?

A person who is far-sighted (hyperopia) needs which lens?
items.e: The focus is behind the retina; a converging lens moves it forward.

items.q: Which device uses two converging lenses to see very small objects?
items.e: The objective lens makes a real image that the eyepiece magnifies.

items.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths 30 cm and −25 cm are placed in contact. What is the focal length of the combination?
What is the power of a lens of focal length 20 cm?
An astronomical telescope has an objective of focal length 160 cm and an eyepiece of 4 cm. What is its magnifying power in normal adjustment?
items.e: m = fo/fe = 40.0; the tube length is 164 cm.

items.q: What does the iris do?
c: it carries signals to the brain
it controls the size of the pupil and so how much light enters
items.e: In bright light the pupil gets smaller.

items.q: What is the blind spot of the eye?
c: the place where the optic nerve leaves the retina, with no light receptors
the coloured part of the eye
items.e: We do not notice it because the brain fills in the gap.

items.q: What is the image in a camera or the eye like?
items.e: Real images can be focused on a screen or sensor.
